scope: Theorem 3.1 (Local metric extension) of the manuscript “Smooth anisotropic uniqueness in the Calderón problem from one boundary patch” (preprints/Smooth-Anisotropic-Uniqueness-in-the-Calderon-Problem-from-One-Boundary-Patch-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 365 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 1ec46ed64206d12d), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 10. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let n ≥ 3. Let (N1, g1) and (N2, g2) be smooth compact connected Riemannian manifolds with nonempty smooth boundary, with Dirichlet Green functions G1, G2. Identify two interior harmonic coordinate neighborhoods with one neighborhood Ω ⊂ Rn of 0. Suppose an open W ⊂ Ω contains, near 0, one side of a smooth hypersurface through 0, and suppose g1 = g2 on W, G1(x, y) = G2(x, y) (x, y ∈ W, x ̸= y). Suppose there are finitely many smooth pairs ua j harmonic for gj on Ω, agreeing on W, whose first-side coordinate Hessians at 0 span {H ∈ Sym2 (Rn ) : gij 1 (0)Hij = 0}. Then the two coordinate metrics agree on a neighborhood of 0.
